title: Julie Craven wins again in court
article: For more than a decade, Julie Craven has been locked in a legal battle over the estate of her estranged husband who killed their son in 2006.
With a judge's ruling released this month, an end appears likely, says the Brantford woman's lawyer.
"I believe this is now the end of it, even though about a third of what she's owed has still not been paid," said Michael Jaeger, who has been working on the case since 2008.

Craven has been fighting to get funds from the estate of Andrew Osidacz. In his will, Osidacz named as beneficiaries his brother, Michael, and mother, Elizabeth Osidacz. Michael Osidacz became executor of his brother's estate in March 2006.
In the most recent court proceeding, which was heard over two days in May, Michael Osidacz was ordered to personally pay various costs and outstanding balances of $117,067 to Craven.
Justice Michael Gibson also ordered the two sides to try and settle any further legal costs between themselves.
"All he had to do was cut a cheque and he never would," Jaeger said of Michael Osidacaz.

In 2017, the matter was decided in Craven's favour, with the trial judge excoriating Michael Osidacz for carrying out a personal "vendetta" against Craven to stop her from getting any funds from the estate.

"Defendant Michael Osidacz was found by the trial judge to have raised 'totally irrational and reckless' defences and to have used the litigation process as a 'vendetta' to 'harass' the plaintiff in a 'reprehensible' manner," summarized Gibson in his ruling.
Jaeger said Osidacz had used countless delays to keep from paying Craven.
"Every possible defence was raised against Julie at trial and with no evidence," he said. "It's been a frustrating process for many people. Most cases like this are resolved out of court."

On March 18, 2006, Jared was visiting his father when Andrew Osidacz stabbed and killed the boy and injured Osidacz's girlfriend and her child. Andrew Osidacz then went to Craven's home and terrorized her for 45 minutes before police arrived and shot him as he raised a knife over her chest.
Although Osidacz's will left everything he had to his brother and mother, the court said Craven was entitled to financial compensation.

Ontario Court Justice Thomas Lofchik ruled that Michael Osidacz "subjected an impoverished, grieving mother who had just nearly been killed by the perpetrator of the heinous murder of her nine-year-old son (to) a litigation 'strategy' of denial, deflection and ultimately blame."

Lofchik ordered Michael Osidacz to release funds from the estate, to personally repay $71,000 plus interest - money that he had used from his brother's estate to fight Craven from getting funds - and to pay more than $169,000 in personal costs to Craven
Osidacz appealed the decision but later abandoned the appeal.
In 2018, he made arrangements to make instalment payments but short-changed the agreed-upon amounts.
In 2020, Craven was able to get a garnishment against Osidacz, resulting in an additional $5,350.
Osidacz tried to fight that garnishment but it was dropped when he didn't show up for cross-examination on the motion.
Jaeger said no amount of money can begin to make his client "whole".
"Obviously, Julie has been affected horribly by all this," he said. "They haven't forgotten what happened and never will forget.
"It's been a tragic and unfortunate case."
